sonnet.problem: The question comes before the facts it asks about. Card 1 never mentions the crowd or Zacchaeus's size, and verse 3 is only told on card 3 after this question. The statement also carries its own answer. Card 3 then retells the same fact, so the baker can only answer by luck, and one fact gets both a question and a retelling.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. / A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it. / Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: Card 5 has just told that Zacchaeus climbs the sycamore, and card 4 already asked what he does. Card 6 asks about the climb again, which repeats the fact from the card before it and the answer already shown on card 4.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it. / An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: Card 11 already asks whether the people were happy, and its answer shows they weren't. Card 12 asks about the same verse 7 grumbling and puts 'begin to grumble' in its question. It re-asks the same point.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.
